notice.text: This call is recorded and transcribed. You can ask the business for a copy of your recording.

writer_rules: Vehicle makes and models are fine, but only the ones in the brief. Do not state facts about real vehicles (defects, ratings, exact prices); prices are rough. A VIN is only ever its last six characters.

scenarios.label: Sales inquiry
scenarios.brief: The caller asks whether a particular new model and trim is in stock, roughly what it costs, and whether they can test drive it. The salesperson answers in general terms, asks a qualifying question, and offers a test drive at a later time.

scenarios.label: Service appointment
scenarios.brief: The caller books routine service (an oil change, a tire rotation, a brake inspection, or a check engine light). The advisor asks for the vehicle and mileage and offers a later day and time, with a shuttle or loaner if it fits.

scenarios.label: Recall question
scenarios.brief: The caller got a recall notice in the mail and asks whether it applies, whether it costs anything, and how long it takes. The advisor looks it up from the last six characters of the VIN, confirms the repair is free, and books it. Keep the recall generic: no defect claims about a real model, no campaign number.

scenarios.label: Trade-in
scenarios.brief: The caller wants to know what their current vehicle is worth as a trade-in. The salesperson asks for the year, mileage and condition, explains that a firm number needs an in-person appraisal, and invites them in.

scenarios.label: Parts order
scenarios.brief: The caller asks the parts counter for a part or accessory (all-weather floor mats, wiper blades, a cabin air filter, a spare key fob), its price and whether it is in stock. The specialist checks and arranges pickup or an order.

scenarios.label: Recording request: copy
scenarios.brief: After the recording notice, the caller asks why calls are recorded, who can hear them, and how to get a copy of their recording. The advisor explains plainly, says the caller can have a copy, and passes the request to the office manager. The caller may add a small service question.

scenarios.label: Recording request: deletion
scenarios.brief: The caller is uncomfortable that the call is recorded and asks for the recording of this call to be deleted. The salesperson notes the request for the manager who handles recordings, promises nothing they cannot do, and asks whether the caller still wants help.

scenarios.label: Hang-up on hold
scenarios.brief: The caller starts asking about a vehicle, the salesperson asks them to hold while they find the right person, and the caller hangs up before anyone comes back, muttering that they will try somewhere else.

scenarios.label: Screened robocall
scenarios.brief: An automated prerecorded sales pitch calls the sales line. The salesperson answers; the recording plays a generic pitch for business energy savings that names no company. The call is cut off by the line's screening announcement.

scenarios.label: Wrong number
scenarios.brief: The caller meant to reach someone else (the person named under People, or a kind of business, never a named one). The salesperson says they have the wrong number, and the call ends politely and quickly.

scenarios.label: After hours
scenarios.brief: The call comes in after the dealership has closed and is answered by its after-hours answering service on its behalf. The attendant gives the hours, takes a name, callback number and reason, and says the right department will call back when it opens.

scenarios.label: Voicemail
scenarios.brief: No one picks up. The first business turn is the advisor's recorded voicemail greeting. The caller leaves a message with their name, vehicle, reason and callback number.

screen.announce: We can't take this call on this line. Goodbye.
